entries.text: After the party returned to the Guild hall in Aegis City, Vallie announced that the Guild would put them forward for the C-rank exam, with Domas presenting written terms and Ellie laying out forms while Tobias watched from behind the counter. Max Nightriver asked Fiana if she would call him a friend, and she delightedly agreed, calling him one of her favorite adventurers and offering free drinks at the tavern for the night. When Max asked about Jasira, Fiana described her as a complicated friend with a high wall around her, a weight she carries, and a habit of expecting people to fail her. Vallie told Max she trusted him to get the job done but not to be sentimental, and Domas said Max owed him nothing, asking only that he live to see his next rank. Max told Fiana she was the closest thing to family he had in the city, and she declared herself his sister in the city. Fiana then explained that Jasira saw Max as a pampered noble, but that her contempt was mixed with recognition of a shared darkness, and advised patience.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's face lights up, her blue eyes widening as she lets out a delighted laugh. She wipes her hands on her apron and steps forward, closing the distance between them.
"Friend? Oh, I'd call you more than that!" Fiana beams, her freckled cheeks flushing. "You're officially one of my favorite adventurers now. Anyone who can keep their head when things go sideways—and looks half as good doing it—is someone I want in my corner."
She gestures toward the tavern's bar with a grin. "Tavern's on me for the rest of the night. We can celebrate your new rank or your survival, or both—your choice."
Max Nightriver: Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression softens, a flicker of something complex passing through her eyes before she leans back against the polished wood of the bar. "Jasira?" She swirls the cider in her glass, watching the bubbles rise. "She's... complicated."
"We're friends," Fiana says slowly, "but the kind where you have to walk on eggshells sometimes. She's got a wall around her—high and thick—and most people just give up trying to climb it. Me? I've always liked a challenge." She shrugs, though there's a tension in her shoulders. "She's the best ranger I've ever seen, but there's always this... weight she carries. Like she's waiting for someone to fail her."
Max Nightriver: Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
Vallie: Vallie's blue eye fixes on Max Nightriver, considering, before she lets out a short bark of a laugh. "Kid, you've got the instincts of a predator and the patience of a spider. I've watched you work." She crosses her arms, her black eyepatch shifting as her expression goes serious. "Trust is a heavy word. I don't give it out like beer tokens."
*She leans in closer, her sharp teeth glinting.*
"But I trust you to get the job done. That's what counts in the Guild." A heavy hand lands on Max's shoulder—not too rough, but firm enough to leave a bruise. "Now quit being all sentimental and sign the damned forms before Domas starts chewing my ear about paperwork."
Max Nightriver: Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
Domas: Domas pauses mid-turn, his red eyes meeting Max's with an unreadable expression. He slowly lowers the clipboard, setting it on the counter with a soft tap.
"You owe me nothing," he says, his voice measured and quiet enough that only a few nearby can hear. "The road is not a place for debts. If you wish to repay me, then live to see your next rank up." He gives a single, curt nod—a gesture of acknowledgement between equals. "That is all the gratitude I require."
*He retrieves his clipboard and glances at the forms Ellie has laid out, waiting.*
Max Nightriver: Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
Adolion Narrator: The words hang in the air between them, soft and heavy. Fiana freezes, her hands still gripped around the rag she'd been using to wipe the bar. Her blue eyes search Max's face, and for a heartbeat, the cheerful mask slips.
"Family..." Fiana breathes the word like it's fragile glass. Her expression softens completely, and she sets the rag down. "You know, most people who come through here just see a barmaid. Someone to pour their drinks and laugh at their jokes." She reaches out, resting her hand briefly over Max's on the cool wood of the bar. "But you actually *see* me."
*She straightens up, a determined look settling on her freckled face.*
"Then you've got a sister in this city now. Someone who'll keep you fed, keep your secrets, and kick your ass if you start acting too much like a brooding hero." Fiana gives his hand a small squeeze before pulling back. "Tavern's still on me tonight. Come on, sit. Tell me what's really going through that head of yours."
Max Nightriver: Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana pauses mid-pour, the cider swirling in her pitcher. She sets it down on the counter with a quiet thud and leans against the bar, her expression growing contemplative.
"Honestly?" Fiana sighs, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as if making sure no one is listening. "She thinks you're a pampered noble who doesn't understand what it means to *earn* something. She sees the Nightriver name and her shoulders tighten up like you've just insulted her ancestors." She drums her fingers on the wood. "But there's more to it. I've seen them in the same room—how she watches you when she thinks you're not looking. It's not just contempt."
*Fiana shakes her head, a wry smile touching her lips.*
"It's like... she recognizes something in you that she doesn't want to admit. Some kind of darkness or weight that matches her own. That's why you clash. She'd rather fight you than face whatever it is that makes her see herself in you." She picks up the pitcher again. "Still, I wouldn't suggest trying to 'get along' with her right now. Just... be patient. Elves like Jasira take a long time to thaw out."
